title: Paloma and the Protocol
premise: Mirabel Brightwater, a clone who inherited both her original's shipping route and the unsolved murder case that ended her, runs cargo between two worlds whose war has severed all contact. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers it carries proof of who killed the first Mirabel — and a message that could end the war if she can deliver it before either government silences it. Pursued by both fleets and haunted by memories that are not hers, she must choose between obeying the protocol that defines her existence and trusting the enemy pilot who once loved her original. In the end she delivers the message at terrible cost, exposing the murderer and forcing peace, but chooses exile over inheritance, becoming no one's copy but her own.
about_author: Freya Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that could not speak directly. She writes from a coastal town where the fog comes in on schedule, like a signal.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She runs the silent corridor between Veyra and Calloway Station, navigating embargo zones while reciting inherited memories of the original's murder. Establishes her loneliness and the legal limbo clones occupy. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A distress broadcast arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct since the Founding Wars; her ship's archive is one of few that can parse it. The message names coordinates inside the war zone. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the first thrill of purpose.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashbacks in the original's voice. Reviewing her predecessor's murder file, she finds the case was closed by the same magistrate now leading Veyra's war council. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Waited
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Intercepted by Calloway pilot Dario Sen, who mistakes her for the original — his former lover. He lets her pass but warns her both governments have flagged her ship. Emotional beat: the ache of being loved as someone else.

chapters.title: Protocol Over Heart
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. He reports her position as duty demands, then falsifies the log to buy her time, torn between oath and old love. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into commitment.

chapters.title: What the Message Says
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Decoded fully, the signal contains the original's hidden testimony: evidence the magistrate orchestrated the murder to ignite the war, plus terms for armistice. Emotional beat: terror — she now carries the thing worth killing for.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Rise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and a Veyra hunter-killer captain ordered to destroy her. She threads an asteroid shoal while the magistrate publicly brands her a clone saboteur. Emotional beat: hunted, betrayed by her own world.

chapters.title: The Court That Isn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Sheltering among smugglers who run justice outside the law, she convenes an improvised tribunal of witnesses to the original's death. Dario arrives to stand with her. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity; justice rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: Deliver or Die
chapters.summary: Climax, Mirabel's POV. She broadcasts the testimony and armistice terms simultaneously to both worlds during the fleets' final confrontation, as the magistrate's forces close in and Dario takes fire shielding her transmitter. Emotional beat: sacrifice against the clock.

chapters.title: No One's Copy
chapters.summary: Resolution, Mirabel's POV. The magistrate falls, cease-fire holds, and the law offers her the original's name and estate. She declines, keeps her own, and departs with Dario on a new route into unclaimed space. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into selfhood.
